name: Youvarlakia Avgolemono (Greek Beef and Rice Meatballs in Lemon Sauce)
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Rice is built into the meatballs and the egg-lemon sauce adds protein, so this eats as a full dinner rather than a soup. Everything is board-mapped and cheap. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated, and portioning needs to be thick (less broth) to hold 500+ cal. | HARVEST: Published figures are 486.7 cal and 18.8 g protein. Source sections: Broth (3), Meatballs (9), Avgolemono (2), To Serve (3).
intro_html: Youvarlakia are Greek meatballs with the rice mixed right into the raw meat, so the grains swell as they simmer and the meatballs end up studded and tender. Then comes avgolemono, the egg and lemon sauce that Greek cooks have been using to thicken broth for centuries. No flour, no cream, just eggs whisked with lemon and tempered slowly into the hot liquid until it turns silky and pale. Get the tempering right and it is magic. Get it wrong and you have made lemon egg drop soup, which is still edible but not the goal.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 5 cups dry: ~$1.15. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.88. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $31.25 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.23 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $33.96 across 14 servings, roughly $2.43 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $15.02 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $48.98. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.23 a bowl for Greek meatballs in a silky lemon sauce that uses eggs instead of cream to get there.
shop_smart: Rice in the meatballs is a deliberate stretch and a delicious one. It replaces bread crumbs, costs less, and gives the texture that makes these youvarlakia instead of plain meatballs.
Eggs do the thickening, so skip the cream aisle entirely. Avgolemono is one of the cheapest ways ever invented to make a rich sauce.
Fresh mint is the biggest non-meat line on this list. It is also worth it, and mint grows like a weed in a pot if you want to stop buying it.
Bottled lemon juice is fine here. The sauce needs acid volume more than fresh zing, and the bottle costs a fraction of a bag of lemons.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground beef with the dry rice, finely grated yellow onion, chopped fresh mint, salt, and black pepper until just combined.
Roll the mixture into evenly sized meatballs, keeping them a little smaller than you think, since the rice expands.
Bring a large pot of water with the olive oil and a good amount of salt to a gentle simmer.
Lower the meatballs in, cover, and simmer gently until the rice inside is fully cooked and the meatballs are firm. Do not let it boil hard or they break apart.
Lift the meatballs out with a slotted spoon and keep the cooking broth at a bare simmer.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice in a bowl until frothy, then ladle in hot broth a little at a time while whisking constantly. This tempering step is the whole trick.
Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the pot off the heat, stir until the broth thickens and turns pale, then return the meatballs and season to taste.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and divide by 14. Count out the meatballs evenly first, then top up each container with sauce by weight. Every bowl lands near 580 calories with 28 grams of protein. Reheat gently on low, because avgolemono will curdle if you blast it.

upsell_html: Bright, silky Greek dinners for about $2.23 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Greek youvarlakia avgolemono rebuilt for 14-serving meal prep: rice-studded beef meatballs in a silky egg and lemon sauce. 580 calories, 28g protein, about $2.23 per serving.
head.keywords: youvarlakia, avgolemono, greek meatballs, egg lemon sauce, greek meal prep, rice meatball soup
steps: Mix the beef with dry rice, grated onion, mint, and seasoning.
Simmer them gently in salted water with olive oil until the rice is cooked through.
Lift the meatballs out and keep the broth at a bare simmer.
Whisk eggs with lemon juice and temper in hot broth a ladle at a time.
Stir the tempered mixture back into the pot off the heat, return the meatballs, and portion into 14 containers.
